newsitem.title: CANADA: UGG raises Canada wheat crop forecast, cuts canola.
newsitem.headline: UGG raises Canada wheat crop forecast, cuts canola.

text.p: United Grain Growers said it raised its forecast for western Canadian wheat production in the 1996/97 (Aug/July) crop year but cut canola output projections on wet, cold harvest conditions.
UGG forecast wheat output of 29.09 million tonnes, up slightly from an earlier projection of 28.61 million and well above Statistics Canada's 1995/96 estimate of 23.85 million.
"At first it looked like a lot of wheat would grade number one and two. Now it looks like there's going to be more number three and feed wheat," UGG analyst Mike Jubinville said.
The forecast was based on a survey of UGG elevator managers September 23-25, when rain and snow delayed harvest progress and caused cereals to bleach and sprout, he said.

Canola production in western Canada this year was projected at 4.88 million tonnes, down from UGG's previous forecast of 5.01 million and sharply below StatsCan's 1995/96 estimate of 6.37 million. Farmers seeded less acres to canola.
"Canola yields declined in Alberta and also in Saskatchewan on these weather problems while yields improved in Manitoba. Quality's a concern. We're looking at an average crop," Jubinville said.

Barley production was projected at 15.56 million tonnes, up from UGG's previous forecast of 15.51 million and sharply up from StatsCan's 1995/96 estimate of 12.11 million. Farmers seeded more acres to barley this spring.
"We'll have more feed barley and less malt barley because of this weather," Jubinville said.

Oats production was projected at 4.42 million tonnes, up from UGG's previous forecast of 4.19 million and sharply higher than StatsCan's 1995/96 estimate of 2.56 million. Farmers seeded more acres to oats.
